items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: I think Benny, I think I met Benny Carter, if I'm thinking correctly, at that time.

ctx.x: Did the negotiations take a long time? It seems like I remember a lot of fund raising and campaigning at the time of working for the amalgamation.

Well, I wasn't here at the time this happened. This was in the '50s when it happened, and I wasn't here at that time. See, I was travelling at the time, and I missed all of that, but there was an awful lot and there are a lot of people, several people that really should bet credit. Marl Young and Buddy Collette and Benny Carter and Red Callendar. And these guys were, you know, they were very, very instrumental in really getting the show on the road. And it was something that would have had to happen in later…

Of course they had some opposition, from what they tell me. In fact I think some of the older members that are still around, they naturally did not see the advantage, you know. They were so used to going down to the old union. But the wonderful force behind the whole thing really won over, and it became a very marvelous thing for everybody. It was advantageous to everybody concerned, really; particularly to the black musicians, because they -- I don't think at the time that they were in a position to really…
